title: Wire signed offline bundle metadata into generated support bundle
author: Ethan Park
body: Context: With signed offline bundles, Support/SEs frequently need to answer "did verification run" and "what exactly was verified" from a support bundle alone (esp. in air-gapped environments where customers share a tarball via offline transport). Today the support bundle includes installer logs and config, but it does not summarize the offline bundle’s manifest/signature state, leading to longer back-and-forth (SUP-31844) and mis-triage when transport corrupts artifacts (SUP-31892). This PR adds a structured summary file and a small amount of diagnostic output so that a support bundle can stand alone for first-pass triage without exposing sensitive customer data. What this changes: (1) Adds a new support bundle attachment: support/bundle-verification.json containing the last-known offline bundle verification result, plus key metadata pulled from the signed manifest and verifier. (2) Includes the raw verification error code + remediation hint (not the full stack trace) to align with the installer’s verification error taxonomy. (3) Captures bundle identity fields needed to correlate to release artifacts: bundle_build_id, bundle_version, manifest_digest_sha256, signature_digest_sha256, signer_key_id, trust_store_version, and installer_version. (4) Adds a "verification_context" block that records whether verification ran during preflight, whether break-glass override was used, and any detected time-skew handling path (without recording the host clock). Safety/redaction: no file paths outside the bundle root are recorded; no customer tokens/URLs are included; the trust store content is not dumped, only the configured trust store version/id and the selected key id. Implementation notes: the support bundle generator now consumes the same in-memory VerificationReport object returned by preflight (or loads the persisted report if present) and writes a stable JSON file using canonical key ordering for diffs. If verification has never been run, the support bundle records status=unknown and includes next steps. Testing: unit tests cover "success", "hash mismatch", "unknown key", "not yet valid" and "break-glass" cases; integration test verifies support bundle output is produced in air-gapped mode. Release note: none (internal supportability improvement), but docs/runbook owners have been notified to reference the new file in triage steps.
commits: supportbundle: add bundle-verification.json attachment and writer
preflight: persist verification report for support bundle reuse
verifier: expose signer key id + signature digest in VerificationReport
tests: add fixtures for verification failure mapping + support bundle output
docs: update internal SUPPORT.md triage section for signed bundles
conversation: Dev Patel (review): Can we make sure Support has a single place to look without parsing logs? Suggest a top-level "status" plus "reason_code" and a short "next_steps" string.
Ethan Park (author): Added top-level status + reason_code + next_steps. Mapped next_steps from existing error taxonomy so it stays consistent with CLI output.
Logan Wright (review): Please confirm we’re not emitting anything that could be considered customer environment PII (hostnames, internal mount paths). Also avoid including the entire trust store.

Ethan Park (author): Confirmed: no hostnames, no absolute paths, no trust store dump. Only trust_store_version + selected signer_key_id. Added a unit test asserting no "path:" keys and no "trusted_keys" array is emitted.

Marcus Lin (review): From a security perspective, include manifest digest + signature digest so we can detect replay/tamper from the support bundle. Also ensure the file is clearly marked as derived from verification, not a new source of truth.

Ethan Park (author): Added manifest_digest_sha256 + signature_digest_sha256. File header comment is not possible in JSON, but added "generated_by" and "source" fields (e.g., source=preflight_verification_report) and documented in SUPPORT.md.
Owen Phillips (review): In SUP-31892 we saw customers using zip/unzip that altered files. Can we surface "bundle_path_transport_warning" when we detect common corruption patterns?

Ethan Park (author): I didn’t add heuristics here (risk of false positives), but I did include the normalized error mapping and next_steps that explicitly calls out "re-transfer bundle, avoid tools that modify permissions/line endings" for hash mismatch cases.
Dev Patel (approval): This will materially reduce first-response time. Approved once CI is green.
Logan Wright (approval): Looks good; thanks for keeping the redaction tight.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved; security requirements met.
Ethan Park (author): Re-ran integration tests after addressing a flaky temp-dir assertion; all green.
